rubric_items.reason: All eight acceptance criteria and the story intent map to REQ-1..REQ-13; sorting/searching and reason entry are out of scope with reasons.
Most REQs atomic and checkable, but REQ-8 bundles filter, date range and paging, and REQ-9 cannot be met alongside REQ-4 for a Cancelled row with a NULL reason.
Every known status cites the ticket line, the baseline or an IDE answer; REQ-4 and REQ-7 correctly cite A-01 and A-02; all claims check out against generated context.
The ticket-vs-schema clash (always a reason vs nullable column) was asked as Q-01, answered in A-01 and recorded as a mismatch; no baseline clash found.
Two precise questions with real options and proposed defaults, both answered; no needless blocking.
Plain wording; glossary terms Cancelled, Scheduled, Completed, No-show, Dashboard, Medical history used consistently.

findings.text: REQ-9 says every row under the Cancelled filter shows a reason, but REQ-4 (from A-01) says a Cancelled row with a NULL reason shows "-". The two REQs contradict; a tester cannot satisfy both.

cites.quote: When the list is filtered by Cancelled, every row shows a reason
For a Cancelled appointment whose `cancellation_reason` is empty (NULL), the column shows "-".

findings.suggested_fix: Reword REQ-9: filtering by Cancelled shows each row's stored reason, or "-" where none is stored (per REQ-4/A-01); cite A-01.

findings.text: REQ-8 is compound: it bundles three separate behaviours (status filter, date range, paging) in one requirement.

cites.quote: The column follows the list's `status filter`, date range and paging

findings.suggested_fix: Split REQ-8 into one REQ each for status filter, date range and paging, each with its own checkable condition.

cites.quote: A cancelled appointment always has a reason of up to 300 characters, entered when it is cancelled;
Medical history appears only on the patient's own page, never in lists, the dashboard or logs.
An appointment called off before it took place, with a reason
